# react-html-content-editor

> A React HTML + CSS content editor with a live preview, an integrated rich-text
> WYSIWYG mode, auto-save, fullscreen, and a composition API. Code editing works
> with zero editor dependencies and upgrades to Monaco (the VS Code editor) via one
> prop. Everything ships from a single package: `react-html-content-editor`.
> This file is optimized for AI coding agents: it is self-contained — you can use
> the library correctly from this file alone, without fetching anything else.

- Package: `react-html-content-editor` (npm), version 2.0.0+ (the `/monaco` entry point and the `codeEditor` prop require 2.0.0; in 1.x Monaco was built in and always installed)
- Peer deps: `react` >=18, `react-dom` >=18, `lucide-react`
- Optional peer deps (Monaco only): `@monaco-editor/react` ^4.7, `monaco-editor` >=0.55 — needed ONLY if you import `react-html-content-editor/monaco`
- License: MIT. Repo: https://github.com/adrianomaringolo/react-html-content-editor
- Entry points: `react-html-content-editor` (main) and `react-html-content-editor/monaco` (Monaco adapter only)
- Module formats: ESM (`index.mjs`) + CJS (`index.cjs`), types included. Tree-shakeable; main entry ~21 KB gzip JS + ~7 KB gzip CSS.

## Setup (required)

```bash
npm install react-html-content-editor
# peer deps, if not already present:
npm install react react-dom lucide-react
# OPTIONAL — only for Monaco-powered code panes:
npm install @monaco-editor/react monaco-editor
```

You MUST import the stylesheet once in your app, or the editor renders unstyled:

```tsx
import "react-html-content-editor/dist/style.css";
```

The edited value is always this shape:

```ts
interface ContentValue { html: string; css: string }
```

`ContentEditor` is controlled: pass `value` and `onChange`. It is NOT sanitized —
see "Security" below.

## Code editor: textarea vs Monaco

Monaco is OPTIONAL. Default (no extra install): the HTML/CSS panes render
`TextareaCodeEditor` — a textarea with a line-number gutter (documents up to
2,000 lines), Tab/Shift+Tab indent-outdent, indentation-preserving Enter,
light/dark palettes and preview scroll sync. No syntax highlighting; the Format
action is hidden because there is nothing to format with.

To use Monaco, install the optional peers and pass the adapter. It lives in a
SEPARATE entry point — this is what keeps Monaco out of projects that do not want
it, so never import it from the main entry:

```tsx
import { ContentEditor } from "react-html-content-editor";
import { MonacoCodeEditor } from "react-html-content-editor/monaco";

<ContentEditor value={value} onChange={setValue} codeEditor={MonacoCodeEditor} />;
```

Both accept identical props, so switching is a one-line change.

Any component implementing `CodeEditorProps` works as `codeEditor`:

```ts
interface CodeEditorProps {
  defaultValue: string;                 // uncontrolled seed; report edits via onChange
  language: "html" | "css";
  theme: string;                        // "vs-dark" | "vs-light"
  options?: Record<string, unknown>;
  onChange: (value: string) => void;
  onReady?: (handle: CodeEditorHandle | null) => void;  // handle on mount, null on unmount
  className?: string;
  ariaLabel?: string;
}

interface CodeEditorHandle {
  focus(): void;
  format(): boolean;                    // false when unsupported
  getScrollTop(): number;
  getMaxScroll(): number;
  setScrollTop(top: number): void;
  onScroll(listener: () => void): () => void;   // returns unsubscribe
}
```

Set `MyEditor.canFormat = false` when the implementation cannot reformat; the
toolbars then hide the Format action.

`TextareaCodeEditor` follows Monaco's `vs` / `vs-dark` palettes (from the `theme`
prop) and can be restyled with `--rhce-code-bg`, `--rhce-code-fg`,
`--rhce-code-gutter-bg`, `--rhce-code-gutter-fg`, `--rhce-code-selection` and
`--rhce-code-font`. These do nothing under `MonacoCodeEditor`, which paints its
own surface.

## Quick start (default layout)

Batteries-included editor: toolbar, HTML/CSS code editors, live preview,
fullscreen, keyboard shortcuts. Just pass `value`/`onChange`. The code panes use
the built-in dependency-free `TextareaCodeEditor` unless you pass `codeEditor`
(see "Code editor: textarea vs Monaco").

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { ContentEditor } from "react-html-content-editor";
import "react-html-content-editor/dist/style.css";

export function App() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState({
    html: "<h1>Hello</h1>",
    css: "h1 { color: teal; }",
  });
  return <ContentEditor value={value} onChange={setValue} height="500px" />;
}
```

### ContentEditor props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `ContentValue` | — | Required. `{ html, css }`. |
| `onChange` | `(value: ContentValue) => void` | — | Required. Fires on any edit. |
| `onSave` | `() => Promise<void>` | — | Enables the save button + Ctrl/Cmd+S. |
| `isSaving` | `boolean` | `false` | External saving state. |
| `htmlLabel` / `cssLabel` | `string` | `"HTML"` / `"CSS"` | Tab/button labels. |
| `className` | `string` | `""` | Applied to the container. |
| `height` | `string \| number` | `"400px"` | Number ⇒ px. |
| `defaultTab` | `"html" \| "css"` | `"html"` | Initial code tab. |
| `editorOptions` | `Record<string, unknown>` | `{}` | Merged into the code editor options (Monaco naming). |
| `codeEditor` | `CodeEditorComponent` | `TextareaCodeEditor` | Code editor implementation. Pass `MonacoCodeEditor` from `react-html-content-editor/monaco` for Monaco. |
| `theme` | `"vs-dark" \| "vs-light"` | `"vs-dark"` | Code editor theme. |
| `error` | `string` | — | Error message shown below the editor. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | Opt into composition mode (see below). |
| `defaultMode` | `"code" \| "wysiwyg"` | `"code"` | Initial mode (composition). |

Keyboard: Ctrl/Cmd+S = save, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+F = format, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+M = fullscreen, Esc = close fullscreen.

## Composition API (assemble the editor from parts)

Pass children to `ContentEditor` to switch to composition mode. Without children
the default layout above renders unchanged (fully backwards compatible). Each pane
reads shared state from context and decides its own visibility, so order is free.

```tsx
import {
  ContentEditor,
  ContentEditorToolbar,
  ContentEditorBody,
  ContentEditorCode,
  ContentEditorPreview,
  ContentEditorWysiwyg,
} from "react-html-content-editor";

<ContentEditor value={value} onChange={setValue} height="520px">
  <ContentEditorToolbar />
  <ContentEditorBody>
    <ContentEditorCode />
    <ContentEditorPreview />
    <ContentEditorWysiwyg />
  </ContentEditorBody>
</ContentEditor>
```

Parts:
- `ContentEditorToolbar` — mode switch (Code/Visual, shown only when a `ContentEditorWysiwyg` is present), view toggles, HTML/CSS tabs, format & save. Props: `className?`, `children?` (children replace the left group; built-in right-side actions are hidden).
- `ContentEditorBody` — responsive split/stacked layout container. Props: `className?`, `children`.
- `ContentEditorCode` — HTML/CSS code editors. Visible in `code` mode. Props: `className?`.
- `ContentEditorPreview` — live HTML+CSS preview. Visible in `code` mode. Props: `className?`.
- `ContentEditorWysiwyg` — rich-text surface bound to the HTML value; adding it makes the toolbar show the Code/Visual switch. The `css` value is applied to the surface via a `<style>` tag. Props: `placeholder?`, `minHeight?` (`string|number`), `className?`, `children?` (compose your own `WysiwygToolbar`/`WysiwygContent`; default toolbar used if omitted).
- `useContentEditorContext()` — hook exposing shared state to custom toolbar children: `{ value, onChange, onHtmlChange, onCssChange, onSave, saveStatus, hasUnsavedChanges, isSaving, mode, setMode, showEdit, showPreview, toggleEdit, togglePreview, activeEditor, setActiveEditor, formatHtml, formatCss, canFormat, theme, htmlLabel, cssLabel, codeEditor, ... }`. Throws if used outside `<ContentEditor>`.

Also exported (advanced/manual wiring): `ContentEditorProvider`, `ContentEditorShell`.

`ContentEditorMode = "code" | "wysiwyg"`. `ViewMode = "edit" | "preview" | "split"`. `EditorType = "html" | "css"`.

## Standalone WYSIWYG editor

A self-contained rich-text editor over an HTML string (no code/CSS panes).
Compound components — include only the controls you need, in any order.

```tsx
import {
  Wysiwyg, WysiwygToolbar, WysiwygContent, WysiwygSeparator,
  WysiwygBold, WysiwygItalic, WysiwygUnderline, WysiwygStrikethrough,
  WysiwygHeading, WysiwygParagraph, WysiwygBlockquote,
  WysiwygUnorderedList, WysiwygOrderedList, WysiwygAlign,
  WysiwygLink, WysiwygUnlink, WysiwygFontSize, WysiwygClearFormatting,
} from "react-html-content-editor";

const [html, setHtml] = useState("<p>Hi</p>");

<Wysiwyg value={html} onChange={setHtml}>
  <WysiwygToolbar>
    <WysiwygHeading level={1} />
    <WysiwygParagraph />
    <WysiwygSeparator />
    <WysiwygBold />
    <WysiwygItalic />
    <WysiwygFontSize />
    <WysiwygUnorderedList />
    <WysiwygOrderedList />
    <WysiwygAlign value="left" />
    <WysiwygLink />
  </WysiwygToolbar>
  <WysiwygContent placeholder="Start writing…" minHeight="320px" />
</Wysiwyg>
```

- `Wysiwyg` props: `value?` (controlled) OR `defaultValue?` (uncontrolled), `onChange?(html)`, `disabled?`, `className?`, `children`.
- `WysiwygContent` props: `placeholder?`, `minHeight?` (`string|number`, default `"240px"`), `className?`, `aria-label?`.
- Named controls take `{ className?, title? }` (`NamedControlProps`). Parametrized ones:
  - `WysiwygHeading` — `level: 1|2|3|4|5|6` (required).
  - `WysiwygAlign` — `value: "left"|"center"|"right"|"justify"` (required).
  - `WysiwygAlignMenu` — single alignment control: the trigger shows the alignment applied to the selection and opens a picker (left/center/justify/right, composed from `WysiwygAlign`). Props: `className?`, `title?`.
  - `WysiwygLink` — `getUrl?: () => string | null` (defaults to `window.prompt`).
  - `WysiwygHeadingMenu` — H1–H6 + paragraph grouped in one dropdown; trigger shows the current level. Props: `levels?`, `className?`, `title?`.
  - `WysiwygFontSize` — dropdown of preset sizes; `options?: WysiwygFontSizeOption[]`.
  - `WysiwygFontSizeInput` — numeric input to type an exact size in px (applies `font-size: Npx` to the selection); `min?`, `max?`.
  - `WysiwygFontFamily` — dropdown; `options?: WysiwygFontFamilyOption[]` ({label,value}).
  - `WysiwygTextColor` — swatch picker (`foreColor`); `colors?: string[]`.
  - `WysiwygClearColor` — reset text color to inherited default.
  - `WysiwygHighlight` — swatch picker (`hiliteColor`); `colors?: string[]` (include `"transparent"` to clear).
  - `WysiwygEmoji` — emoji picker (inserts via `insertText`); `emojis?: string[]`.
  - `WysiwygSpecialChar` — special-character picker; `characters?: string[]`.
  - `WysiwygFullscreen` — toggle fullscreen for the editor (Fullscreen API on the root).
  - `WysiwygLinkEditor` — not a toolbar button; place inside the editor. When the caret is in a link, a portaled bar appears to open / edit (change URL) / remove it. Props: `getUrl?: (current) => string | null`, `className?`.
  - `WysiwygDropdown` — reusable popover primitive the grouped controls are built on. Props: `title`, `trigger`, `triggerAriaLabel?`, `triggerData?`, `active?`, `closeOnSelect?`, `children`.
  - `WysiwygWordCount` — read-only counter (not a button); `render?: ({words,characters}) => ReactNode`.
  - `WysiwygImage` — insert an image. Default: file picker → embed as base64 data URI (no server). Pass `getSrc?: () => string | null | Promise<string | null>` to insert by URL/link instead. `accept?` defaults to `"image/*"`.
  - `WysiwygImageUpload` — file picker → `upload(file)` → insert the returned URL. `upload: (file: File) => Promise<string>` (required); `accept?` (`"image/*"`), `onError?`. Disables itself + shows a spinner while uploading.
  - `WysiwygImageResizer` — not a toolbar button; place it inside `<Wysiwyg>`/`<ContentEditorWysiwyg>`. Clicking an image shows a floating bar (rendered in a body portal, anchored to the image) with size presets AND a pixel-width input that set the image `width` (height auto). Props: `options?: WysiwygImageSizeOption[]` (default S 25% / M 50% / L 100%), `showReset?` (default true), `showPixelInput?` (default true), `resetTitle?`, `className?`.
- Inline: `WysiwygBold`, `WysiwygItalic`, `WysiwygUnderline`, `WysiwygStrikethrough`, `WysiwygSubscript`, `WysiwygSuperscript`, `WysiwygInlineCode`. Block: `WysiwygParagraph`, `WysiwygBlockquote`, `WysiwygCodeBlock`, `WysiwygHorizontalRule`, `WysiwygIndent`, `WysiwygOutdent`. Lists: `WysiwygUnorderedList`, `WysiwygOrderedList`. Utilities: `WysiwygUnlink`, `WysiwygClearFormatting`. History: `WysiwygUndo`, `WysiwygRedo`. Layout: `WysiwygToolbar`, `WysiwygSeparator`.

## Building custom WYSIWYG controls

All controls are built on `WysiwygControl`. Use it for your own. Works inside a
standalone `Wysiwyg` or a `ContentEditorWysiwyg`.

`WysiwygControlProps`: `command: string`, `value?: string`, `useCss?: boolean`,
`title: string`, `isActive?: (ctx) => boolean`, `onActivate?: () => void`,
`children`, `className?`, `disabled?`.

```tsx
import { WysiwygControl, useWysiwygContext } from "react-html-content-editor";
import { Highlighter, CalendarPlus } from "lucide-react";

// 1) Declarative — wrap any execCommand, define your own active state:
function WysiwygHighlight() {
  return (
    <WysiwygControl
      command="hiliteColor" value="#fde047" useCss title="Highlight"
      isActive={({ queryValue }) => {
        const c = queryValue("hiliteColor") || queryValue("backColor");
        return !!c && c !== "transparent" && c !== "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)";
      }}
    >
      <Highlighter size={16} aria-hidden="true" />
    </WysiwygControl>
  );
}

// 2) Bespoke behaviour — read context, run your own action:
function WysiwygInsertDate() {
  const { exec } = useWysiwygContext();
  return (
    <WysiwygControl command="insertText" title="Insert date"
      onActivate={() => exec("insertText", new Date().toLocaleDateString())}>
      <CalendarPlus size={16} aria-hidden="true" />
    </WysiwygControl>
  );
}
```

`useWysiwygContext()` exposes: `exec(command, value?, useCss?)`, `commit(html)`,
`isActive(command)`, `queryValue(command)`, `value`, `disabled`, `editorRef`.
Common `execCommand` ids: `bold`, `italic`, `underline`, `strikethrough`,
`insertUnorderedList`, `insertOrderedList`, `formatBlock` (value `<h1>`…`<h6>`,
`<p>`, `<blockquote>`), `justifyLeft|Center|Right|Full`, `createLink`, `unlink`,
`fontSize`, `foreColor`, `hiliteColor`, `removeFormat`, `insertText`.

GOTCHA (important): in any custom control, call `e.preventDefault()` on
`onMouseDown` so clicking the button does not collapse the editor's text
selection before your command runs. `WysiwygControl` already does this.

## Recipes

Auto-save:
```tsx
<ContentEditor value={value} onChange={setValue} onSave={async () => { await save(value); }} isSaving={saving} />
```

Start composition in visual mode:
```tsx
<ContentEditor value={value} onChange={setValue} defaultMode="wysiwyg"> … </ContentEditor>
```

Style the toolbar (buttons are real `<button>`s; active toggles expose `aria-pressed="true"`):
```tsx
<ContentEditorToolbar className="my-toolbar" />
```
```css
.my-toolbar button[aria-pressed="true"] { background: #7c3aed; color: #fff; }
```

Replace the toolbar's left group with your own controls (built-in actions hidden):
```tsx
function ModeSwitch() {
  const { mode, setMode } = useContentEditorContext();
  return (<><button onClick={() => setMode("code")}>Code</button>
           <button onClick={() => setMode("wysiwyg")}>Visual</button></>);
}
<ContentEditorToolbar><ModeSwitch /></ContentEditorToolbar>
```

## Security

The preview and the WYSIWYG surface render HTML with `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.
Sanitize untrusted HTML before passing it in (e.g. DOMPurify):
```tsx
import DOMPurify from "dompurify";
<ContentEditor value={{ html: DOMPurify.sanitize(value.html), css: value.css }} onChange={setValue} />
```
